premise: Pachycephalosaurus can't wait for Fern's curled-up fiddlehead to open: he bounces, he begs, he huffs; Archaeopteryx says wait; the rain falls, the sun comes out, and slowly, slowly, it unrolls into a brand-new frond.
inspiration: The old tale of the farmer who tugged his sprouts to make them grow faster (Mencius), turned: nobody tugs, and waiting is the trick.
lesson: Some things open in their own time.
learning: A new fern leaf grows curled up tight and slowly unrolls.

en-US.title: Not Yet, Said Fern
en-US.text: {fern:enter} [playfully] On top of Fern sat two curled-up fronds, round and tight as snail shells. {pachycephalosaurus:enter} {pachycephalosaurus:go to fern} {sfx:boing} Pachycephalosaurus came bouncing over. {pachycephalosaurus:live bounce} "When will they open? Now? NOW?" {fern:face happy} "Not yet," giggled Fern. On a branch of the tree fern, {archaeopteryx:enter} {archaeopteryx:go to branches} Archaeopteryx {archaeopteryx:live preen} was tidying her feathers. [warmly] "A fern takes its time," she said. {pachycephalosaurus:face sad} [sighs] Pachycephalosaurus huffed. The next day, {canvas:rain 0.6} {sfx:rain} pitter-patter, it rained. "Now?" asked Pachycephalosaurus. {fern:wobble} "Not yet," said Fern, drinking up the rain. {canvas:rain stop} The day after that, {canvas:sunshine 0.8} the sun came out, warm and bright. And slowly… slowly… {fern:live unfurl hold} one of the curls began to unroll, into a brand-new frond, fresh and green. {pachycephalosaurus:face surprised} [whispers] "It's opening," whispered Pachycephalosaurus. He didn't bounce. He didn't huff. {pachycephalosaurus:face happy} He just watched. {archaeopteryx:face happy} {archaeopteryx:hop} Even Archaeopteryx stopped to look. Then Pachycephalosaurus looked at the other curl. [excited] "And that one? NOW?" {fern:wobble x2} And Fern laughed so much that all his fronds shook. {canvas:sunshine stop}

es-ES.title: Todavía no, dijo Helecho
es-ES.text: {fern:enter} [playfully] En lo alto de Helecho había dos hojitas enrolladas, redondas y apretadas como conchas de caracol. {pachycephalosaurus:enter} {pachycephalosaurus:go to fern} {sfx:boing} Paquicefalosaurio llegó dando botes. {pachycephalosaurus:live bounce} —¿Cuándo se abren? ¿Ya? ¿YA? {fern:face happy} —Todavía no —se rio Helecho. En una rama del helecho gigante, {archaeopteryx:enter} {archaeopteryx:go to branches} Arqueoptérix {archaeopteryx:live preen} se arreglaba las plumas. [warmly] —Un helecho nunca tiene prisa —dijo. {pachycephalosaurus:face sad} [sighs] Paquicefalosaurio resopló. Al día siguiente, {canvas:rain 0.6} {sfx:rain} plic, ploc, llovió. —¿Ya? —preguntó Paquicefalosaurio. {fern:wobble} —Todavía no —dijo Helecho, bebiéndose la lluvia. {canvas:rain stop} Y al otro día {canvas:sunshine 0.8} salió el sol, calentito y brillante. Y despacito… despacito… {fern:live unfurl hold} una de las hojitas empezó a desenrollarse, hasta convertirse en una hoja nueva, fresca y verde. {pachycephalosaurus:face surprised} [whispers] —Se está abriendo —susurró Paquicefalosaurio. No botó. No resopló. {pachycephalosaurus:face happy} Solo miró. {archaeopteryx:face happy} {archaeopteryx:hop} Hasta Arqueoptérix se paró a mirar. Luego Paquicefalosaurio se fijó en la otra hojita. [excited] —¿Y esa? ¿YA? {fern:wobble x2} Y Helecho se rio tanto que le temblaron todas las hojas. {canvas:sunshine stop}
